name: Bristle
description: The burrow's fast chaff — a silverfish out of the wall seams, running the nest's trails and stealing off them, the one thing down here that does not belong to the hive. Three cuts went wrong before this one, and the last two went wrong the same way: the filaments were drawn as separate rods, and five thin rods radiating off a small oval is an asterisk at the size this is actually seen at, not a creature. This system reads big simple shapes — the Tracker is one mass with a notch, the Drifter is two wings, the Molt is a shell with a lit split — so the three tails fuse into one broad plume, notched twice so they stay legible as three. The silhouette is a comet: a hard bright dart with its scale rows cut into it, dragging a fan half again its own length, and nothing else in the game is that shape. Because the plume hangs off a single root it sweeps on one rotation track, with a second brighter fan inside it running about a fifth of a cycle behind — the plume lagging the body that drags it is the whole motion. Cool silver against a roster of warm bone and amber, so it never competes with the Replete or the Porter's brood at a glance, and the palest body here on purpose: it runs on #372d3f earth and the quickest thing on screen must never be the hardest to see. Legs are derived rather than eyeballed — front pair reaching forward, rear pair trailing, middle straight out to the side. Drawn from directly above along +x, because the game turns this body to its heading rather than flipping it, and a top-down body has no up to protect. Gameplay radius 7.

elite.description: Marked: the shell bleaches past bone, the plume opens wider and brighter than the body dragging it, and the signal it stole off the trail is burning on its own back.

skitter.description: the fastest gait on the roster. The dart itself barely moves — it is not what you are looking at — while the plume sweeps behind it and the fan inside the fan arrives about a fifth of a cycle late, which is the difference between a trail and a wag. Sampled eight times and interpolated straight, because the default ease brings a value to a stop at every key it passes and a sweep built out of those stops flicks instead of trailing.
